analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation plus a submodule pointer bump. changelog.d/gptoss-decode-command-buffers.md (new, lines 1-3) and docs/architecture/inference.md (date bump on line 3, new 'GPT-OSS decode command buffers' section at head lines 4816-4826) describe GPT-OSS plain decode committing a Metal command buffer every 100 operations with no input-size bound, while prefill keeps MLX defaults. The docs claim bitwise-identical outputs. No authorization, attestation, key custody, wire protocol, prefix-cache (T-041) or add-on (TB-012/TB-013) behavior is changed or described as changed. The surrounding doc excerpts are unchanged context. The cache posture (30-minute TTL, HMAC lookup tags, account-scoped salt) is not touched, so the T-041 mitigations are intact.

The unreviewed security-relevant item is the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer move (7933a0fa to 63baac23). Only the pointer is supplied, with no diff of the submodule. It presumably carries the GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers and CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding implementation, but that is not verifiable here. This is inside TB-007, which holds decrypted prompt data. Unreviewed risks: larger or unbounded per-buffer operation counts could change GPU memory pressure or cancellation and completion latency (T-010, T-029). Residual GPU data lifetime (T-028) and cache or KV handling could also be affected. The 'bitwise identical' and partition-independence claims are unverified. Since the code change is outside the evidence, I record this as a coverage limit rather than a finding. A reviewer with the submodule diff should check memory bounds, cancellation behavior and any change to prompt or KV retention.
